_readme: Controls which Halo MCP tools the voice agent can use. Rules are checked in order; first match wins.
kind: read | create_ticket | add_note | close_ticket | deny. 'match' is a tool name or a glob (* wildcard), case-insensitive.

ticketIdArg names the ticket ID parameter (add_note, close_ticket). omitArgs are hidden from Claude and stripped before the call. fixedArgs are hidden from Claude and always sent with these values (null = not configured, tool hidden). description replaces the tool's own description.
Tools that match no rule are allowed only if the MCP server marks them readOnlyHint=true (and allowReadOnlyAnnotated is true).

Matched to the Halo MCP catalogue (/api/mcp: the generic tools plus CF_Email_User, CF_Resolve_Ticket, CF_User_Details; 25 tools) on dhitsminternal.app.usehalo.com on 2026-11-18. Re-check with `npm run list-tools` if the endpoint changes.
Write policy agreed for the PoC: create tickets and add notes to the caller's own tickets. Tickets resolved on the call are closed with CF_Resolve_Ticket, limited to tickets created on this call.

rules._why: Public note; limited in code to tickets seen on this call
Describes the API account, not the caller
Tickets assigned to the API account, not the caller's
Only tickets created on this call (resolved on the call); enforced in session.ts. The AI KB-article and closure-review options are hidden and turned off.
Arbitrary ticket actions (close, escalate...); CF_Resolve_Ticket covers closing
Lists every user's email and phone; used only by the pre-call lookup below
Emails the end user and takes a status that could change the ticket
Refreshes matches on a ticket (a write)
Not annotated read-only; the agent can't fill in a catalogue request by phone

identify._readme: Pre-call caller lookup. CF_User_Details takes no args, so it is called once and treated as a full user list; hits are kept only if the user's stored number equals the caller's (site phone fields ignored). The alternative is get_users with { "search": "{phone}" }. Delete this block to let the agent identify the caller itself.

promptNotes: Use the email from the caller lookup as user_email. Only ask the caller for their email if the lookup didn't provide one.

Find the caller's tickets with search_tickets, searching by their email address or name with open_only set to true, or by the ticket number if they have one. Use get_one_ticket for a ticket's history. Only discuss or add notes to a ticket that belongs to the caller.
To find the caller's device, try get_assets with their name. If that finds nothing, ask for the asset tag on the sticker or the model and search with that.
Search the knowledge base with get_knowledge using a few key words from the symptoms, then get_one_article for the full steps.
create_ticket takes the caller's email address, a summary of 70 characters or less, and a description. Leave ticket_type blank.

If the issue was fixed on the call, log a ticket with create_ticket describing what fixed it, then close it with CF_Resolve_Ticket, with a short note saying how it was resolved. You can only close a ticket you created on this call.
add_note_to_ticket adds a public note that the caller can see. Write it as a short, polite update in plain words.
